intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a half-day exploring the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum over 1,500 years, then walk to the stunning Blue Mosque with its six minarets and exquisite Iznik tile interior. Hire a local guide for deeper historical context on Byzantine and Ottoman empires.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Bazaar Food and Culture Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops, then head to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar to sample Turkish delight, saffron, dried fruits, and local spices. Engage with vendors, taste free samples, and soak in centuries of trading culture.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Breakfast in Karaköy
experiences.description: Experience a lavish authentic Turkish breakfast spread known as 'kahvaltı' featuring olives, white cheese, sucuk (spiced sausage), fresh bread, honey, clotted cream, tomatoes, cucumbers, and multiple egg dishes. Join locals at a beloved neighborhood café for a leisurely 2-hour morning ritual that is central to Turkish daily culture.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Harem Tour
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent Topkapi Palace, the administrative and residential center of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Walk through the Imperial Treasury, view sacred relics, and take a guided tour of the Harem quarters to understand the complex social hierarchy and daily life of Ottoman sultans and their court.

experiences.name: Bosphorus Sunset Cruise with Street Food Evening
experiences.description: Take a public ferry cruise along the Bosphorus Strait, the waterway dividing Europe and Asia, passing Ottoman palaces, ancient fortresses, and wooden yalı mansions. After docking, explore Karaköy and Galata waterfront street food stalls for freshly grilled balık ekmek (fish sandwich), simit, and roasted chestnuts as the sun sets over the minarets.
experiences.location: Eminönü Ferry Docks to Bosphorus, Karaköy waterfront

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 22:30. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives at 22:30. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the Havaist airport bus or metro (most budget-friendly option, ~50-70 TRY) to your accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and cheap simit (sesame bread ring) or a döner wrap from a 24-hour street stall near the airport or hotel (~30-50 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport for immediate needs. Download the Istanbul metro app and Google Translate offline Turkish pack before landing. Keep arrival receipts for any transport.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a slow morning at the hotel. Walk along the nearby beachfront promenade to get oriented with the neighborhood. Visit a local bakkal (corner store) to stock up on water, fruit, and snacks for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate beachfront area on foot. Visit any nearby local bazaar or neighborhood market to soak in everyday Istanbul life. If the hotel is near the Asian or European shore, take a short walk to a tea garden (çay bahçesi) and enjoy traditional Turkish tea with a view of the Bosphorus.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearest local neighborhood for dinner. Stroll along the waterfront at sunset. Try a casual local meyhane (tavern) or a simple lokanta (traditional Turkish canteen) for an affordable and authentic first dinner in Istanbul.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or visit a local fırın (bakery) for fresh simit, börek, and tea (~40-60 TRY)
meals.lunch: Street food near the beachfront — try a balık ekmek (fish sandwich) if near the water or a gözleme (savory crepe) from a street vendor (~50-80 TRY)
meals.dinner: Local lokanta offering a set menu of soup, main dish, and salad (~80-120 TRY per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is an orientation day. Get your Istanbulkart (rechargeable transit card) from a nearby metro station or kiosk — it saves significantly on all public transport fares.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to the Sultanahmet (Old City) district — the heart of historic Istanbul. Begin with the Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya), one of the world's greatest architectural marvels, now a mosque with free entry. Dress modestly and bring a scarf. Spend 1.5-2 hours exploring its Byzantine mosaics and Ottoman additions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the square to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) — free entry, closed during prayer times. Admire the six minarets and stunning Iznik tile interior. Afterward, explore the Hippodrome of Constantinople (At Meydanı), an open-air ancient racetrack with the Obelisk of Theodosius, Serpent Column, and German Fountain — all free to view.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Sultanahmet neighborhood streets at dusk. Enjoy the illuminated mosques and historic atmosphere. Find a rooftop restaurant or a simple kebab house on the side streets for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Simit, cheese, olives, and tea at a local çay evi near the hotel (~40-60 TRY)
meals.lunch: Cheap and filling pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) at a local pide salonu near Sultanahmet (~70-100 TRY)
meals.dinner: Adanalı kebab restaurant in Sultanahmet side streets — Adana or Urfa kebab with bread and ayran (~100-140 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Hagia Sophia is free but closes for Friday prayers. The Blue Mosque is free but requires modest dress — scarves are provided at the entrance. Avoid touts near Sultanahmet who offer 'free tours' leading to carpet shops.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Topkapi Palace (Topkapı Sarayı) — the seat of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years. Entrance fee is approximately 500-600 TRY but well worth it for the scale and history. Explore the Imperial Gate, the Harem (separate ticket ~200 TRY), the Treasury with Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond, and the sacred relics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down from Topkapi to the Gülhane Park — Istanbul's oldest public park, free entry and beautifully maintained. Relax among the rose gardens. Then visit the Istanbul Archaeology Museums (Arkeoloji Müzeleri) adjacent to Gülhane, housing the Alexander Sarcophagus and artifacts from across the ancient world (~100-150 TRY).
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the historic Divan Yolu street back toward Sultanahmet. Browse the arasta bazaar (smaller, less touristy than Grand Bazaar) for local crafts. Enjoy an evening tea at a traditional çay bahçesi.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local börek shop — su böreği (water pastry with cheese) and tea (~50-70 TRY)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks from morning or grab a lahmacun (thin Turkish pizza) from a street vendor inside or near Gülhane (~40-60 TRY)
meals.dinner: Kuru fasulye (white bean stew) and rice at a traditional lokanta near Sultanahmet — a classic budget Ottoman comfort meal (~80-100 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is closed on Tuesdays. Arrive early (opens at 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. The Harem tour requires a separate ticket and timed entry — book at the entrance. Comfortable walking shoes are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Entry is free. Wander through the labyrinthine lanes of jewelry, spices, textiles, ceramics, and leather goods. Practice your bargaining skills — prices are always negotiable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes downhill to the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı / Egyptian Bazaar) near Eminönü. Browse stalls of colorful spices, Turkish delight, dried fruits, and nuts. Pick up affordable souvenirs like small spice packets or lokum (Turkish delight). Stroll along the Eminönü waterfront and watch the ferries on the Golden Horn.
day_by_day.evening: Take the famous Galata Bridge walk — fishermen line both sides day and night. Cross to the Karaköy neighborhood on the other side. Explore the hip, artsy streets of Karaköy and Galata for an evening stroll. Head back via ferry or metro.

meals.breakfast: Menemen (scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) at a local kahvaltı salonu near the hotel (~60-80 TRY)
meals.lunch: Street food at Eminönü — balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from the iconic floating boats on the waterfront (~60-80 TRY) with a glass of şalgam (turnip juice)
meals.dinner: Midye dolma (stuffed mussels) from a street vendor on Galata Bridge area as a snack, then a full meal at a Karaköy meyhane with mezze (~100-150 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Beware of pickpockets in crowded bazaar areas. Bargaining is expected and fun — start at 50% of the asking price. The Spice Bazaar is less aggressive for bargaining and good for food souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — arguably Istanbul's most magnificent mosque, built by the legendary architect Sinan in the 16th century. Free entry. Climb the surrounding streets for panoramic views of the Golden Horn and city. Explore the historic külliye (mosque complex) including the tombs of Suleiman the Magnificent and his wife Hürrem Sultan.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the Fatih neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most traditional and conservative districts. Visit the Fatih Mosque and the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque), famous for its stunning Byzantine mosaics (~100-150 TRY entry). Explore the historic Balat neighborhood with its colorful Greek and Jewish heritage houses.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through Balat's charming backstreets lined with antique shops and local cafes. Balat has become a trendy but still affordable neighborhood. Watch the sunset over the Golden Horn from the Balat hillside.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Turkish breakfast spread at a Fatih neighborhood lokanta — olives, cheese, eggs, honey, cream, and tea (~60-90 TRY)
meals.lunch: Köfte (meatball) sandwich from a street stall in Fatih or near Süleymaniye (~40-60 TRY)
meals.dinner: A casual dinner at one of Balat's charming local restaurants — try mercimek çorbası (lentil soup) and a main dish (~90-120 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) may have limited access if restoration work is ongoing — check ahead. Balat is best explored on foot and is very photogenic. Wear comfortable shoes as the streets are cobblestone and hilly.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or tram to Beyoğlu and walk up to Galata Tower (Galata Kulesi) — a medieval stone tower with panoramic 360-degree views of Istanbul (~200-250 TRY entry). Alternatively, enjoy the free view from the surrounding streets. Explore the Galata neighborhood's art galleries and bohemian cafes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up the famous İstiklal Avenue (İstiklal Caddesi) — Istanbul's most famous pedestrian boulevard stretching 1.4 km from Galata to Taksim Square. Browse independent bookshops, vintage stores, music shops, and street performers. Visit the historic Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) and Balık Pazarı (Fish Market) off İstiklal.
day_by_day.evening: Reach Taksim Square and explore the surrounding Cihangir neighborhood — a bohemian enclave with great cafes and street art. Watch the sunset from Cihangir's hillside park with Bosphorus views. Return to hotel via metro.

meals.breakfast: Trendy but affordable breakfast at a Galata cafe — avocado toast or Turkish breakfast plate (~80-120 TRY)
meals.lunch: Döner kebab wrap from a fast-casual spot on İstiklal Avenue (~60-80 TRY)
meals.dinner: Meyhane dinner in Cihangir or Beyoğlu with raki and mezze — budget-friendly set menus available (~120-160 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: İstiklal Avenue is extremely crowded on weekends. The historic red tram runs along İstiklal — a short ride costs one Istanbulkart fare and is a fun experience. Cihangir is popular with expats and has a relaxed vibe.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bosphorus ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy to Üsküdar on the Asian side — one of Istanbul's best budget experiences (~15-20 TRY with Istanbulkart). Arrive in Üsküdar and visit the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque and the famous Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi) visible from the shore (~150-200 TRY to visit the tower by boat).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Üsküdar along the Asian shore to Kadıköy — Istanbul's vibrant, youthful, and less touristy Asian district. Explore the Kadıköy market (Kadıköy Çarşısı) for local produce, cheeses, olives, and street food. Browse the Moda neighborhood's charming streets and waterfront park.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Kadıköy's famous nightlife and food scene on Barlar Sokağı (Bar Street) and surrounding streets. Take the late ferry back to the European side with beautiful illuminated Bosphorus views at night.

meals.breakfast: Simit and tea on the ferry or at an Üsküdar waterfront cafe (~30-50 TRY)
meals.lunch: Kadıköy market food tour — graze on kokoreç (offal sandwich), midye tava (fried mussels), and fresh börek (~80-100 TRY total)
meals.dinner: Moda neighborhood restaurant with fresh fish or a casual meyhane in Kadıköy (~100-140 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: The ferry between European and Asian Istanbul is one of the world's great cheap experiences. Kadıköy is considered more authentic and less touristy than the European side — prices are generally lower. Carry your Istanbulkart for ferry and bus connections.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) in Sultanahmet — a stunning underground Byzantine water reservoir with atmospheric lighting, ancient columns, and the famous Medusa head bases (~250-300 TRY). Arrive early to avoid crowds. Then visit the nearby Binbirdirek Cistern (free or very low cost) — less crowded and equally impressive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Divan Yolu and visit the Column of Constantine (Çemberlitaş) — a free ancient Roman column. Walk to the Nuruosmaniye Mosque and the surrounding hans (historic Ottoman caravanserais). Browse the Sahaflar Çarşısı (Old Book Bazaar) near the Grand Bazaar for secondhand books and prints.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Pierre Loti Café on the hilltop of Eyüp — accessible by a scenic cable car (~30 TRY) or a 20-minute uphill walk. Named after the French novelist, it offers stunning views over the Golden Horn and is a beloved local tradition. Return via the Eyüp Sultan Mosque area.

meals.breakfast: Menemen and fresh bread at a Sultanahmet side-street lokanta (~60-80 TRY)
meals.lunch: Cheap and filling tarhana çorbası (fermented wheat soup) and bread at a traditional soup house (çorba salonu) (~40-60 TRY)
meals.dinner: Eyüp neighborhood lokanta for a traditional Ottoman-style dinner — lamb stew or stuffed vegetables (~90-120 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: The Basilica Cistern is one of Istanbul's most atmospheric sites — bring a light jacket as it's cool underground. Pierre Loti Café has been a local institution for over a century — order traditional Turkish coffee and enjoy the view. Eyüp is a deeply religious neighborhood; dress modestly.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — a group of car-free islands in the Sea of Marmara, a 1-2 hour ferry ride from Kabataş or Eminönü (~50-80 TRY round trip with Istanbulkart). Visit Büyükada (the largest island) with its Victorian mansions, pine forests, and horse-drawn carriages. Rent a bicycle (~100-150 TRY for the day) to explore the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or walk to the hilltop Monastery of St. George (Aya Yorgi) for panoramic views of the Marmara Sea. Explore the island's quiet beaches (May weather permitting) and charming neighborhoods. Browse the small shops and enjoy the peaceful, car-free atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Take the ferry back to Istanbul in the early evening, watching the city's skyline emerge across the water. This is one of Istanbul's most memorable views. Arrive back at the hotel for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hotel or grab simit and tea at the Kabataş ferry terminal (~40-60 TRY)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a waterfront restaurant on Büyükada — grilled fish with salad and bread (~120-160 TRY) or a cheaper balık ekmek from a harbor vendor (~70-90 TRY)
meals.dinner: Simple dinner near the hotel after returning — a neighborhood pide or kebab restaurant (~80-110 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Check the ferry schedule in advance — ferries run regularly but can be crowded on weekends. The Princes' Islands are a beloved escape for Istanbulites. Horse-drawn phaetons are a traditional way to tour but can be expensive (~400-600 TRY for a tour) — cycling is cheaper and more fun.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dolmabahçe Palace (Dolmabahçe Sarayı) on the European Bosphorus shore — the 19th-century Ottoman palace that replaced Topkapi as the imperial residence. Guided tours only (~400-500 TRY). The crystal staircase, 4.5-ton chandelier, and Bosphorus-facing facade are extraordinary. Book tickets online in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Beşiktaş waterfront from Dolmabahçe. Visit the Çırağan Palace (now a hotel but exterior is free to view and photograph). Continue to the Ortaköy neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most picturesque spots with its baroque mosque on the Bosphorus and the Bosphorus Bridge backdrop. Browse the weekend craft market in Ortaköy Square.
day_by_day.evening: Ortaköy is famous for its kumpir (giant baked potato with toppings) — a must-try Istanbul street food. Enjoy dinner in the Ortaköy waterfront area. Watch the illuminated Bosphorus Bridge at night from the waterfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a Beşiktaş neighborhood breakfast cafe (~60-90 TRY)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or a light meal near Dolmabahçe before the tour
meals.dinner: Ortaköy kumpir (baked potato) as a filling street food dinner (~60-80 TRY) plus midye dolma (stuffed mussels) from vendors (~30-50 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires pre-booked timed entry tickets — buy online to avoid queues. Photography inside the palace is restricted. Ortaköy is one of Istanbul's most Instagrammable spots — the mosque with the bridge backdrop is iconic. The area gets very busy on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Turkish and Islamic Arts Museum (Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi) in Sultanahmet — one of Turkey's finest museums with an extraordinary collection of Islamic calligraphy, carpets, ceramics, and manuscripts (~150-200 TRY). Then walk to the Mosaic Museum (Büyük Saray Mozaikleri Müzesi) nearby to see stunning 6th-century Byzantine floor mosaics (~100 TRY).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a relaxed afternoon to visit a traditional Turkish hammam (bathhouse) — a quintessential Istanbul cultural experience. The Çemberlitaş Hamamı (near the Grand Bazaar) is historic and budget-friendly with basic packages from ~400-600 TRY including kese (exfoliating scrub) and soap massage. Alternatively, visit the Cağaloğlu Hamamı for a similar experience.
day_by_day.evening: After the hammam, feel refreshed and relaxed. Enjoy a leisurely final full evening in Istanbul. Return to a favorite neighborhood from the trip — perhaps Kadıköy or Beyoğlu — for a farewell dinner and a last stroll along the Bosphorus.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Turkish breakfast at a Sultanahmet café — full spread with olives, cheese, eggs, tomatoes, and tea (~80-100 TRY)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the museums — mercimek çorbası (lentil soup) and a sandwich (~50-70 TRY)
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at a mid-range lokanta or fish restaurant — try kuzu tandır (slow-roasted lamb) or a fresh Bosphorus fish (~150-200 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: The hammam experience is best enjoyed without rushing — allow 1.5-2 hours. Bring flip-flops and a change of underwear. Tips for the hammam attendants are customary (~100-150 TRY). Book hammam entry in advance during peak tourist season.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul. Pack and check out of the hotel (confirm late checkout if needed). Take one last walk along the beachfront or to a nearby viewpoint to say goodbye to the city. Visit a local pazar (open-air market) if one is running in the neighborhood — great for last-minute affordable food souvenirs like spices, dried figs, or tea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with plenty of time. Use the Havaist bus or metro/rail connection from the city center to Istanbul Airport (~50-80 TRY). Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Browse the airport's duty-free for any last-minute Turkish delight or baklava.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul. Reflect on 13 days of incredible history, culture, and food in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Last Turkish breakfast in Istanbul at a neighborhood fırın or café — simit, börek, and çay (~50-70 TRY)
meals.lunch: Quick bite at the airport or a final street food stop before departure — döner wrap or a pastry (~60-80 TRY)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Airport is very large — allow extra time to navigate between terminals. Keep some Turkish Lira for any last-minute transport or tips. Havaist buses are cheaper than taxis but confirm the schedule. Spend any remaining TRY on food souvenirs as currency exchange back can be costly.

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront district. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack at the hotel bar or order room service — try a classic Turkish 'tost' (toasted sandwich) or lentil soup if available

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you'll arrive late. Confirm your hotel transfer in advance. Exchange some currency or withdraw Turkish Lira at the airport ATM. Rest well for a full Day 2 ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Start gently with a leisurely hotel breakfast overlooking the Bosphorus or beachfront. Afterward, take a short walk along the waterfront promenade near the resort to acclimate to Istanbul's atmosphere and sea air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a short ferry from Bostancı or Kabataş pier. Explore Büyükada, the largest island, by renting a bicycle or taking a horse-drawn carriage. Enjoy charming wooden mansions, pine forests, and stunning sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland by ferry and dine at a local meyhane (traditional Turkish tavern) near the waterfront. Enjoy cold meze platters and fresh fish as the sun sets over the sea.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet — fresh simit, olives, white cheese, eggs, honey, and çay (Turkish tea)
meals.lunch: Simple seafood lunch on Büyükada island — grilled fish sandwich or calamari at a casual island café (approx. 150–250 TRY)
meals.dinner: Waterfront meyhane dinner — try haydari (yogurt dip), stuffed mussels, grilled sea bass, and raki (approx. 400–600 TRY per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets are affordable and scenic. The Princes' Islands are car-free — perfect for a relaxed first full day. Check ferry schedules in advance at IDO or Şehir Hatları websites.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the historic Sultanahmet district (Old City). Begin at the magnificent Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) — one of the world's greatest architectural wonders, originally a Byzantine cathedral, later an Ottoman mosque, now a functioning mosque open to visitors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the square to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii), admiring its six minarets and stunning Iznik tile interior. Then explore the ancient Hippodrome of Constantinople and the nearby Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — an atmospheric underground Roman cistern.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Arasta Bazaar for light souvenir shopping, then enjoy dinner in Sultanahmet at a rooftop restaurant with views of illuminated mosques.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or stop at a street cart for simit with tea near the ferry pier
meals.lunch: Traditional Turkish lunch at a lokanta (worker's restaurant) in Sultanahmet — try İskembe çorbası (tripe soup), rice pilaf, and stuffed peppers (approx. 150–200 TRY)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant in Sultanahmet — Ottoman-style dishes like hünkar beğendi (lamb on eggplant purée) with a Bosphorus view (approx. 400–550 TRY per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hagia Sophia requires modest dress — bring a scarf for women and remove shoes before entering. Arrive early to beat the crowds. The Basilica Cistern charges a small entry fee (~200 TRY). Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapı Palace — the grand seat of the Ottoman Empire for centuries. Explore the Imperial Treasury (home to the Spoonmaker's Diamond and Topkapı Dagger), the Harem quarters, and the sacred relics pavilion. Allow 2–3 hours minimum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to Gülhane Park for a relaxing stroll among rose gardens and centuries-old trees. Then explore the Istanbul Archaeology Museums complex nearby — three museums housing Greek, Roman, and Anatolian artifacts including the stunning Alexander Sarcophagus.
day_by_day.evening: Take a tram to the Eminönü waterfront. Watch locals fish off the Galata Bridge, then dine at one of the famous fish sandwich boats (balık-ekmek) or a traditional restaurant below the bridge.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Casual café inside or near Topkapı Palace grounds — börek (flaky pastry), ayran (yogurt drink), and fresh fruit (approx. 100–180 TRY)
meals.dinner: Balık-ekmek (grilled mackerel sandwich) from the floating boats at Eminönü (~60 TRY) or a sit-down seafood restaurant under Galata Bridge (approx. 350–500 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Topkapı Palace and the Harem require separate tickets. Book online in advance to skip queues. The palace is closed on Tuesdays. Gülhane Park is free and lovely in May when roses bloom.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Browse carpets, ceramics, spices, jewelry, and leather goods. Practice your bargaining skills!
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü — a sensory feast of saffron, dried fruits, Turkish delight, and herbal teas. Pick up food souvenirs. Then cross the Golden Horn to Karaköy and explore the trendy waterfront neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take the historic Tünel funicular up to Beyoğlu and stroll along İstiklal Avenue — Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard lined with 19th-century European architecture, bookshops, music stores, and cafés. Catch live music at a meyhane in the Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a traditional Turkish breakfast spread at a local kahvaltı salonu near Sultanahmet
meals.lunch: Spice Bazaar area — try kokoreç (seasoned offal sandwich) or a hearty soup at a street-side lokanta (approx. 100–150 TRY)
meals.dinner: Beyoğlu meyhane dinner — meze, grilled meats, live fasıl music (approx. 400–600 TRY per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. May 19th is Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day — a national holiday with possible parades on İstiklal Avenue. Enjoy the festive atmosphere!

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — the grandest Ottoman mosque in Istanbul, built by architect Mimar Sinan for Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent. Enjoy panoramic views of the Golden Horn from its terrace garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Fatih neighborhood — Istanbul's most traditional and conservative district. Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii) with its breathtaking Byzantine mosaics and frescoes. Walk through the old city walls and the Balat and Fener neighborhoods, known for their colorful houses and Greek Orthodox heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Balat for dinner — this neighborhood has become a hub for artsy cafés and authentic local restaurants. Enjoy a relaxed evening in one of Istanbul's most photogenic quarters.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Süleymaniye area — famous for its bean (kuru fasulye) and rice restaurants; try Darüzziyafe restaurant in the mosque complex (approx. 200–300 TRY)
meals.dinner: Balat neighborhood restaurant — try Albanian-style liver (Arnavut ciğeri), pickled vegetables, and local wine (approx. 300–450 TRY per person)

day_by_day.notes: Chora Church may require advance ticket booking. Balat and Fener are best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes on the cobblestone streets. This area is very authentic and less touristy.

day_by_day.morning: Take a relaxing Bosphorus cruise — book a public Şehir Hatları ferry from Eminönü for a scenic journey up the strait past Ottoman palaces, wooden yalıs (waterfront mansions), fortresses, and two continents. The full cruise goes up to Anadolu Kavağı.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Anadolu Kavağı on the Asian shore. Hike up to the medieval Yoros Castle for sweeping views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Browse the small fishing village and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Eminönü and head back to the hotel. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the resort or at a local neighborhood restaurant — a perfect rest after a full day on the water.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up for the boat day
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch in Anadolu Kavağı — grilled turbot, sea bream, or lobster at one of the village's waterfront fish restaurants (approx. 350–500 TRY per person)
meals.dinner: Neighborhood lokanta near the hotel — home-cooked Turkish comfort food like İmam bayıldı (stuffed eggplant), lentil soup, and baklava (approx. 200–300 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry is very affordable (~50–80 TRY round trip) and far more authentic than private tours. Check the Şehir Hatları schedule — the full Bosphorus cruise runs a few times daily. Bring sunscreen and a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul — take a ferry from Kabataş or Beşiktaş to Kadıköy, Istanbul's vibrant, bohemian Asian district. Explore the Kadıköy Market (Kadıköy Çarşısı) — a wonderful food market full of fresh produce, cheeses, olives, and local delicacies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Moda — a charming seaside neighborhood in Kadıköy with tree-lined streets, vintage shops, and independent cafés. Walk along the Moda coastline promenade with views back toward the European shore. Visit the Haydarpaşa Train Station — a stunning neo-Gothic German-built terminus on the Bosphorus.
day_by_day.evening: Stay on the Asian side for dinner in Kadıköy — one of Istanbul's best neighborhoods for authentic, affordable food. Then take the late ferry back, enjoying the city lights from the water.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a classic Turkish breakfast at a Kadıköy kahvaltı café upon arrival
meals.lunch: Kadıköy Market area — assemble a picnic of local cheeses, cured meats, fresh bread, and olives from market stalls (approx. 150–200 TRY)
meals.dinner: Kadıköy restaurant — try kuzu tandır (slow-roasted lamb), piyaz (white bean salad), and künefe (cheese dessert) at a classic Anatolian restaurant (approx. 300–450 TRY per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kadıköy is beloved by locals and less touristy — a great day to experience real Istanbul life. The Bağdat Avenue shopping street is nearby if you want to browse. Ferry back is scenic at night.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace — the lavish 19th-century Ottoman palace on the European Bosphorus shore, where Atatürk spent his final days. Marvel at the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier (4.5 tons) and opulent state rooms. Guided tours are mandatory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a taxi to the nearby Beşiktaş neighborhood. Visit the Naval Museum (Deniz Müzesi) with its collection of imperial caïques (royal rowboats) and Ottoman maritime history. Explore the lively Beşiktaş market area and waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the upscale Nişantaşı neighborhood for an evening of window shopping along its elegant boutique-lined streets, then enjoy a sophisticated dinner at one of its acclaimed restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Beşiktaş neighborhood — try midye dolma (stuffed mussels from street vendors) and a döner wrap from a local spot (approx. 100–150 TRY)
meals.dinner: Nişantaşı restaurant — modern Turkish cuisine with a contemporary twist; try dishes like slow-cooked lamb shank with bulgur pilaf (approx. 450–650 TRY per person)

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires advance booking — tours fill up quickly. The palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays. Photography restrictions apply inside. Wear modest clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Experience a traditional Turkish hammam (bathhouse) — visit the historic Çemberlitaş Hamamı or Çağaloğlu Hamamı in Sultanahmet, both dating back to the Ottoman era. Enjoy a full ritual of steam, exfoliation (kese), and foam massage — a deeply cultural and rejuvenating experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts (Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi) on the Hippodrome — housing extraordinary collections of Ottoman manuscripts, carpets, ceramics, and calligraphy. Then explore the Küçük Ayasofya (Little Hagia Sophia) — a beautiful 6th-century Byzantine church converted into a mosque.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening dinner in Kumkapı — Istanbul's famous seafood district with dozens of lively restaurants, street musicians, and a festive atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hammam — mercimek çorbası (red lentil soup) and fresh bread at a neighborhood lokanta (approx. 100–150 TRY)
meals.dinner: Kumkapı seafood feast — grilled sea bass, octopus salad, shrimp güveç (casserole), and cold meze with live music (approx. 400–600 TRY per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book your hammam session in advance, especially in May. Prices range from 500–800 TRY for a full traditional experience including kese and massage. Bring flip-flops and a change of underwear. Drink plenty of water afterward.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Galata Tower — the iconic medieval Genoese tower in Karaköy offering 360-degree panoramic views of Istanbul, the Golden Horn, and the Bosphorus. Arrive early to avoid queues. Then explore the charming Galata neighborhood with its antique shops and steep cobblestone streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Galata Bridge on foot and explore the Eminönü and Sirkeci area. Visit the historic Sirkeci Train Station — the legendary terminus of the Orient Express. Then take a short walk to the Egyptian Obelisk and explore the lesser-visited Byzantine and Ottoman monuments around Sultanahmet.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Sema ceremony (Whirling Dervishes performance) — a UNESCO-recognized spiritual ritual of the Mevlevi Order, performed regularly at the Hodjapasha Cultural Center or Sirkeci Station. A deeply moving cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a Karaköy breakfast at one of the neighborhood's trendy cafés — avocado toast meets Turkish cheese spread
meals.lunch: Eminönü area — try a steaming bowl of işkembe (tripe soup) or a hearty pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) at a casual restaurant (approx. 150–200 TRY)
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner near Sirkeci — Ottoman cuisine at a traditional restaurant; try mantı (Turkish dumplings with yogurt and butter) and baklava (approx. 300–450 TRY per person)

day_by_day.notes: Galata Tower tickets should be booked online in advance (~300 TRY). The Sema ceremony typically starts at 19:00 or 21:00 — book tickets in advance online (~400–600 TRY). Photography is usually permitted but flash is not.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Edirne or stay local and visit the Eyüp Sultan Mosque — one of the holiest sites in Istanbul, built over the tomb of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, companion of the Prophet. Take the cable car up to Pierre Loti Hill for stunning Golden Horn views and tea at the historic café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Miniaturk park on the Golden Horn — a fascinating outdoor museum with 1:25 scale models of Turkey's most important historical monuments. Then visit the Rahmi M. Koç Museum nearby — an excellent industrial museum housed in an Ottoman anchor foundry, with vintage cars, trains, and maritime exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a relaxed final full evening. Enjoy sunset drinks at the hotel's beachfront bar, then a special farewell dinner at a fine waterfront restaurant near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Pierre Loti Café on the hill — tea, Turkish coffee, and light snacks with a Golden Horn panorama (approx. 100–150 TRY)
meals.dinner: Waterfront seafood restaurant near the resort — splurge slightly on your penultimate evening; try levrek (sea bass) baked in salt crust and chocolate fondant for dessert (approx. 500–700 TRY per person)

day_by_day.notes: Eyüp Sultan Mosque requires modest dress. The cable car (teleferik) to Pierre Loti is a fun experience and costs very little. Miniaturk is great for a quick overview of Turkish heritage — allow 1.5 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely final hotel breakfast. Take a last stroll along the beachfront promenade near the resort. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping nearby — pick up Turkish tea sets, lokum (Turkish delight), or hand-painted ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (standard checkout is 12:00 — arrange late checkout if needed). Depending on your flight time, visit a nearby café for a final Turkish coffee and reflection on your trip. Head to the airport with ample time — Istanbul Airport is approximately 45–60 minutes from the city center.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Istanbul. Board your return flight with wonderful memories of 13 days exploring one of the world's most captivating cities.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor the olives, white cheese, honey, and çay one last time
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a local café near the hotel — try a gözleme (stuffed flatbread) or menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) (approx. 150–200 TRY)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in, security, and immigration at Istanbul Airport. Keep some Turkish Lira for last-minute purchases or tips. Store your luggage at the hotel concierge if you have time to spare before departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport on flight UA at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind with a welcome amenity (Turkish delight, herbal tea, or a glass of raki) provided by the resort. Light room service available.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining from the resort's curated menu — opt for a light mezze platter and warm lentil soup to ease into Turkish cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport meet-and-greet and private chauffeur transfer in advance. Confirm early check-in or luggage storage if needed. Rest well — a full day of exploration begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort's terrace restaurant overlooking the Bosphorus or beachfront. Afterward, take a private guided tour of the Hagia Sophia — arrive early to beat crowds. Explore the Byzantine mosaics, the Imperial Gallery, and the recently restored Ottoman-era calligraphy medallions with a specialist art historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Sultanahmet Mosque (Blue Mosque) for an intimate guided visit. Continue to the ancient Hippodrome of Constantinople to view the Obelisk of Theodosius, the Serpent Column, and the German Fountain. Visit the Istanbul Archaeology Museums — one of the world's most underrated collections — with a private expert guide.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the historic Sultanahmet waterfront promenade. Dinner at Matbah Restaurant, located within the Ottoman Palace Hotel, serving authentic Ottoman imperial cuisine in a refined setting.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast at the resort — simit, white cheese, olives, sucuk, eggs, clotted cream with honey, fresh-squeezed pomegranate juice
meals.lunch: Mezze lunch at Giritli Restaurant near Sultanahmet — famous for its Aegean-style spreads and fresh seafood
meals.dinner: Matbah Restaurant — tasting menu featuring hünkar beğendi (sultan's delight), lamb tandir, and Ottoman-style desserts

day_by_day.notes: Book private guide and Hagia Sophia tickets in advance. Dress modestly for mosque visits (scarves and coverings available at entrance). Sultanahmet district is walkable — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Private tour of Topkapi Palace — explore the Imperial Treasury (home to the Topkapi Dagger and the Spoonmaker's Diamond), the Harem quarters, and the Sacred Relics Chamber. A specialist guide will bring the Ottoman Empire's 400-year reign to vivid life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the adjacent Gülhane Park, one of Istanbul's oldest public parks, in full spring bloom. Cross into the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) for a curated luxury shopping experience — focus on handcrafted jewelry, antique tiles, silk scarves, and bespoke leather goods. A personal shopping concierge can be arranged.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Bosphorus cocktail cruise aboard a private yacht — sail past Dolmabahçe Palace, the Bosphorus Bridge, and the illuminated shoreline. Dinner on the water or return to shore for a reservation at Mikla Restaurant atop the Marmara Pera Hotel for panoramic city views.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with peppers and tomatoes), börek pastries, fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at Havuzlu Restaurant inside the Grand Bazaar — a hidden gem serving traditional Turkish home cooking
meals.dinner: Mikla Restaurant — contemporary Anatolian-Nordic cuisine by Chef Mehmet Gürs; reserve the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Harem tickets must be purchased separately — book in advance. Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Private yacht cruise should be booked 48–72 hours ahead through the resort's concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — the magnificent underground Byzantine water reservoir, recently renovated with atmospheric lighting. Follow with a private tour of the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood, home to the finest surviving Byzantine mosaics in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Fener and Balat neighborhoods on foot with a local cultural guide — discover colorful Ottoman-era houses, the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate, and vibrant street art. Browse independent antique shops and artisan studios. Visit the Bulgarian St. Stephen Church, a remarkable all-iron neo-Gothic church on the Golden Horn.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a traditional hammam (Turkish bath) experience at the hotel's luxury spa — full ritual with kese exfoliation, foam massage, and aromatherapy oil treatment. Quiet dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fresh simit with tahini and grape molasses, cheese board, herbal teas
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local meyhane (tavern) in Balat — try stuffed mussels (midye dolma), arnavut ciğeri (Albanian-style liver), and cold mezze
meals.dinner: Resort fine-dining restaurant — seasonal tasting menu with Aegean-inspired dishes and premium Turkish wines from Kavaklidere or Chamlija

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for Fener and Balat — streets are cobblestoned and hilly. Book the hammam session in advance. Chora Church may have limited access depending on ongoing restoration — verify before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a private boat from the resort or a luxury ferry from Kabataş. Arrive at Büyükada (the largest island), rent a horse-drawn carriage or bicycle, and explore the pine-forested hills, Belle Époque mansions, and the Greek Orphanage (Prinkipo Palace).
day_by_day.afternoon: Picnic lunch prepared by the resort on the island's hillside or dine at a waterfront fish restaurant. Explore the smaller island of Heybeliada by bicycle — visit the historic Greek Orthodox seminary and enjoy serene coastal views. Swim in the clear Marmara Sea if weather permits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by private boat as the sun sets over the city skyline. Dinner at Poseidon Restaurant in Bebek — one of Istanbul's most celebrated seafood establishments on the Bosphorus.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — light and energizing before the ferry
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket prepared by the resort chef, or seafood lunch at Büyükada Balık Restaurant on the island
meals.dinner: Poseidon Restaurant, Bebek — grilled sea bass, lobster, and seasonal Aegean fish with Bosphorus views

day_by_day.notes: Princes' Islands are car-free — transportation is by carriage or bicycle only. Bring sunscreen, hats, and light layers. Private boat charter from the resort is the most comfortable option. Confirm ferry schedules in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Dolmabahçe Palace on the European shore of the Bosphorus — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman imperial palace featuring 285 rooms, 46 halls, and the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier (4.5 tons). Explore the Selamlık (men's quarters) and Harem sections with an expert historian.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or drive to the upscale Beşiktaş and Nişantaşı neighborhoods. Visit the Istanbul Naval Museum for maritime history. Browse high-end Turkish fashion boutiques and concept stores in Nişantaşı — Istanbul's answer to Milan's fashion district. Visit the Çırağan Palace grounds for afternoon tea.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Tuğra Restaurant inside the Çırağan Palace Kempinski — one of Istanbul's most prestigious dining experiences, serving classic Ottoman cuisine in a palace setting overlooking the Bosphorus.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — kaymak (clotted cream) with honey, fresh pastries, Turkish coffee
meals.lunch: Afternoon tea and light bites at Çırağan Palace Kempinski's terrace café — finger sandwiches, Ottoman pastries, premium teas
meals.dinner: Tuğra Restaurant — Ottoman imperial tasting menu with dishes such as lamb shank in rose water, stuffed quince, and palace-style baklava

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires separate tickets for Selamlık and Harem — purchase both. Photography restrictions apply inside. Reserve Tuğra Restaurant well in advance as it books quickly. Nişantaşı shopping is best on weekday afternoons.

day_by_day.morning: Culinary immersion morning — join a private Turkish cooking class with a renowned local chef. Learn to prepare classic dishes: börek, imam bayıldı (stuffed eggplant), slow-cooked lamb, and Turkish delight from scratch. Class held in a traditional Ottoman-style kitchen in the Beyoğlu district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the vibrant Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü with your guide — taste and purchase premium saffron, sumac, dried figs, Turkish tea, and specialty lokum (Turkish delight). Walk across the Galata Bridge and watch local fishermen. Climb the historic Galata Tower for 360-degree panoramic views of Istanbul.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the bohemian Karaköy and Beyoğlu neighborhoods. Visit İstiklal Avenue at dusk. Dinner at Nicole Restaurant in Tomtom Suites — a Michelin-recommended rooftop restaurant with creative modern Turkish cuisine and spectacular city views.

meals.breakfast: Light resort breakfast before the cooking class
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class — a true farm-to-table (kitchen-to-table) experience
meals.dinner: Nicole Restaurant — seasonal tasting menu with local Anatolian ingredients, natural Turkish wines, and rooftop Golden Horn views

day_by_day.notes: Cooking class must be booked in advance — the resort concierge can arrange a private session. Galata Tower has a small entrance fee and can be crowded — visit in the late afternoon for golden hour views. İstiklal Avenue is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the ancient city of Ephesus (fly or drive — approximately 1 hour by flight to Izmir, then 1 hour drive). Private guided tour of the remarkably preserved Roman ruins: the Library of Celsus, the Great Theatre, the Temple of Hadrian, and the Terrace Houses (must-see with private access). One of the best-preserved ancient cities in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby House of the Virgin Mary (Meryem Ana Evi) — a sacred pilgrimage site set in peaceful pine forests. Explore the Ephesus Museum in Selçuk for artifacts not on display at the site. Optional visit to a traditional Turkish carpet weaving atelier for a private demonstration.
day_by_day.evening: Return flight to Istanbul. Light dinner at the resort upon return — allow for rest after a full day of travel and exploration.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast or airport lounge breakfast before the flight
meals.lunch: Lunch at Celsus Restaurant in Selçuk — fresh Aegean mezze, grilled octopus, and local olive oil dishes
meals.dinner: Resort room service or light dining at the resort's terrace — grilled fish, salads, and Turkish wines

day_by_day.notes: Book early morning flight to Izmir (Adnan Menderes Airport) and private car transfer to Ephesus. Pre-book Terrace Houses tickets as they have limited daily capacity. This is a long day — comfortable walking shoes are essential. Consider a private guide fluent in ancient history.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort — enjoy the spa, beachfront, or pool. Optional sunrise yoga session on the terrace. Late breakfast at leisure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the Sabancı Museum in Emirgan — one of Turkey's finest private art museums, housed in a historic Bosphorus mansion. Rotating exhibitions of Ottoman miniatures, Orientalist paintings, and contemporary Turkish art. Walk through the adjacent Emirgan Park, famous for its tulip gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Drive along the Bosphorus to the charming Arnavutköy neighborhood — lined with 19th-century wooden Ottoman mansions. Dinner at Arnavutköy Balıkçısı — a legendary fish restaurant beloved by Istanbul's elite for decades.

meals.breakfast: Extended resort breakfast — fresh juices, egg station, pastries, and seasonal fruits
meals.lunch: Café lunch at the Sabancı Museum's terrace café — light sandwiches, Turkish coffee, and homemade cakes
meals.dinner: Arnavutköy Balıkçısı — whole grilled turbot, sea bream ceviche, mussel pilaf, and chilled rakı with meze

day_by_day.notes: Check Sabancı Museum's current exhibition schedule before visiting. Emirgan Park is stunning in May with full spring foliage. Arnavutköy is best reached by private car or taxi along the Bosphorus coastal road.

day_by_day.morning: Private Bosphorus boat tour — cruise the strait from its widest point to the narrowest, passing under the Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge, viewing Rumeli Fortress (Rumelihisarı) and Anadolu Fortress (Anadoluhisarı). Stop at the Küçüksu Pavilion (a small Ottoman summer palace) for a guided visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Asian side of Istanbul — take the private boat to Kadıköy, Istanbul's trendiest neighborhood. Browse the vibrant Kadıköy Market (Tarihi Kadıköy Çarşısı) for artisan cheeses, cured meats, fresh produce, and specialty foods. Visit Moda neighborhood for its café culture and sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar in Kadıköy with views of the Marmara Sea. Dinner at Çiya Sofrası — a legendary restaurant celebrated internationally for its encyclopedic regional Anatolian cuisine, preserving recipes from across Turkey.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread with regional Turkish cheeses and house-made jams
meals.lunch: Street food tour of Kadıköy Market — sample kokoreç, balık ekmek (fish sandwich), midye dolma, and fresh ayran
meals.dinner: Çiya Sofrası, Kadıköy — rotating menu of rare Anatolian dishes; try the lamb tandir, tarhana soup, and herb-stuffed pastries

day_by_day.notes: Bosphorus boat tour should be booked as a private charter through the resort. Kadıköy Market is best experienced with a local food guide. Çiya Sofrası is casual but world-renowned — no reservation needed but arrive early.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Süleymaniye Mosque — the masterpiece of Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan, built for Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent. Explore the mosque complex including the türbes (mausoleums) of Suleiman and his wife Hürrem Sultan. Walk through the surrounding historic bazaar streets of the university district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts (Ibrahim Pasha Palace) in Sultanahmet — housing one of the world's finest collections of Islamic art, including Seljuk carpets, Iznik ceramics, and illuminated manuscripts. Continue to the Arasta Bazaar near the Blue Mosque for artisan shopping — high-quality Iznik tiles, handmade ceramics, and silk textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Private whirling dervish (Sema) ceremony — arrange an exclusive viewing of the Mevlevi Sema ritual at a historic tekke (lodge) or cultural center. A profoundly spiritual and visually mesmerizing experience. Dinner afterward at Asitane Restaurant — specializing in meticulously researched Ottoman palace recipes.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Turkish tea, fresh bread, white cheese, and seasonal preserves
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi — Istanbul's most iconic köfte (meatball) restaurant, operating since 1920
meals.dinner: Asitane Restaurant, Edirnekapı — Ottoman tasting menu including dishes from 15th-century palace records; try the almond-stuffed chicken and rose petal desserts

day_by_day.notes: Süleymaniye Mosque is one of Istanbul's most architecturally significant sites — allow at least 90 minutes. Private dervish ceremony should be arranged through the concierge for an authentic, non-touristy experience. Asitane is near Chora Church — combine if revisiting.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive behind-the-scenes visit to the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (recently relocated to its stunning new Renzo Piano-designed building in Karaköy) — arrange a private curator-led tour of the permanent collection and special exhibitions focusing on Turkish contemporary and modern art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury afternoon at leisure — return to the resort for a private spa treatment (choose from a signature Ottoman hammam ritual, deep tissue massage, or a Bosphorus-view couples' treatment). Alternatively, take a private helicopter tour over Istanbul for aerial views of the city's iconic skyline, bridges, and coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Neolokal Restaurant in SALT Galata — one of Istanbul's most acclaimed fine-dining establishments. Chef Maksut Aşkar's cuisine celebrates forgotten Anatolian ingredients and techniques in a beautifully restored Ottoman bank building.

meals.breakfast: Special resort breakfast — champagne, freshly baked pastries, smoked salmon, and premium Turkish cheeses
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort's pool bar — mezze, grilled vegetables, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Neolokal Restaurant — chef's tasting menu with wine pairing; expect dishes like fermented grain soups, aged lamb, and wild herb desserts

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Modern curator tour requires advance arrangement — contact the museum's education department or use the resort's luxury concierge. Helicopter tour must be booked 48+ hours in advance. Neolokal is one of Turkey's top-ranked restaurants — reserve at least 2 weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — last breakfast at the resort with panoramic views. Take a slow walk along the beachfront or hotel grounds. Visit the resort's gift shop for premium Turkish souvenirs: artisan olive oil, specialty teas, hand-painted ceramics, and premium lokum. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: optional last visit to a nearby landmark or neighborhood. If time allows, stop at the Ortaköy neighborhood — admire the iconic Ortaköy Mosque against the Bosphorus Bridge backdrop, browse weekend artisan markets, and enjoy a final kumpir (stuffed baked potato) or waffle from a street vendor. Private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul. Access the premium airport lounge for a final taste of Turkish hospitality before your flight.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — full Turkish spread with every regional specialty sampled over the trip
meals.lunch: Light bites in Ortaköy or at the airport lounge — Turkish pastries, mezze, and Turkish coffee
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in at Istanbul Airport (IST). The resort concierge can arrange a private luxury transfer, luggage handling, and fast-track airport services. Consider purchasing duty-free Turkish saffron, caviar, or premium rakı as final gifts.

query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026
